bib.title: Impossible Distillation for Paraphrasing and Summarization: How to Make High-quality Lemonade out of Small, Low-quality Models

question: Can a small, off-the-shelf LM that cannot itself paraphrase or summarize be used to distill a high-quality dataset and task model, without a large LLM teacher or human references?
hypothesis: Paraphrastic proximity: a sentence and its paraphrases lie in a proximal subspace of a pretrained LM distribution, so constrained sampling plus critic filtering yields good paraphrase pairs.
contributions: Impossible Distillation framework: pair generation from GPT2-scale LM, critic filtering, student distillation, self-distillation
DIMPLE, a 4M-pair synthetic paraphrase corpus (2M general, 2M biomedical)
Impossible-T5 (770M) beating same-size models trained on larger corpora and ChatGPT-distilled data
Generalisation to syntax-controlled paraphrase and sentence summarization (DIMSUM, 1.5M pairs)

method.summary: Sample 100 next sentences per LM-generated context from GPT2-XL or BioGPT-large, enumerate all pairs, filter with NLI, ROUGE-L, tree-edit-distance and an entailment-graph diversity filter, fine-tune T5-large on 400k pairs, then self-distill: the student paraphrases new teacher-sampled sentences, the same critics filter, and T5-large is fine-tuned again. Controllable variant takes the target constituency tree as extra input; summarization swaps in a one-way entailment filter and a compression-ratio filter.
method.task: paraphrase generation (unconstrained and syntax-controlled) and sentence summarization via critic-filtered self-distillation

datasets.name: DIMPLE (generated)
datasets.size: 4.2M pairs in Table 1 text (4M: 2M general, 2M biomedical); 400k filtered pairs for first student stage
datasets.preprocessing: critic filtering (NLI tau 0.75, ROUGE-L <= 0.75, TED >= 12, diversity filter)

datasets.name: DIMSUM (generated)
datasets.preprocessing: unidirectional NLI >= 0.75, compression ratio < 0.8, diversity filter

training.objective: maximise E[log p(y|x)] over filtered pairs (conditional log-likelihood); controllable model also conditions on tree t

other.self_distillation: one round; student generates y for teacher-sampled x, same critics, fine-tune again

inference.decoding: Pair generation: nucleus sampling, k=100 samples per context; contexts sampled with top_p 0.9
inference.temperature: 0.7 for pair generation; 1.0 for sampling contexts
inference.top_p: 0.9 for contexts; pair-generation top_p not stated
inference.prompting: General-domain contexts prompted with prefix such as 'New York (CNN) -'; BioGPT free-form; ChatGPT baselines zero-shot / 5-shot

metrics.name: iBLEU
metrics.definition: Sun and Zhou 2012 paraphrase BLEU penalising copy

metrics.name: BERT-iBLEU (B-iB)
metrics.definition: iBLEU variant using BERT similarity, Niu et al. 2021

metrics.name: SimCSE cosine, 2/3-gram entropy, MSTTR, Jaccard, TED-3, TED-F
metrics.definition: dataset semantic, lexical and syntactic diversity

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no seeds or significance tests stated. Human eval: 200 MRPC paraphrases per model (100 summaries each for Table 5), six MTurk workers, Krippendorff alpha 0.62, $15/hour.

evidence.quote: Throughout the distillation process, we used 4 Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs.

results.claim: Impossible-T5 gets higher BERT-iBLEU on MRPC than T5 trained on ChatGPT-Para.
results.setup: MRPC, unconstrained paraphrase generation, T5-large student (770M) trained on DIMPLE-derived data, GPT2-XL/BioGPT-large 1.5B teachers; baseline T5 fine-tuned on ChatGPT-Para
results.table: Table 2, row Impossible-T5, column MRPC B-iB (67.1) vs row T5ChatGPT-Para (62.9)

results.claim: Removing self-distillation drops BERT-iBLEU by 3.1 on MRPC.
results.setup: MRPC ablation, student distilled from teacher only
results.quote: BERT-iBLEU in this case degrades by 3.1 from Impossible-T5

results.claim: Applying the same critics to ChatGPT-Para (about 340k pairs left) and training T5-large reaches 64.1 BERT-iBLEU on MRPC, below Impossible-T5 (67.1).
results.quote: In this configuration, BERT-iBLEU on MRPC marks 64.1, improving over the original ChatGPT-Para but still falling behind Impossible-T5.

results.claim: DIMPLE (4.2M pairs) beats ParaBank1 (57.0M) on all three diversity and similarity families; SimCSE cosine similarity 87.68 vs 81.77.
results.setup: Dataset comparison, Table 1 (cosine similarity, 2/3-gram entropy, MSTTR, Jaccard, TED-3, TED-F)
results.table: Table 1, row DIMPLE (4.2M), column Cosine Sim.

results.claim: DIMPLE syntactic diversity TED-F is 29.84 vs 20.15 for ChatGPT-Para.
Syntax-controlled paraphrase on ParaNMT-small: Impossible-T5 iBLEU 11.2 vs ChatGPT 5-shot 9.0, but ROUGE-L is lower than the T5 ParaBank baselines.
results.setup: ParaNMT-small, syntactic exemplar parsed to tree and fed to model
results.note: Paper: 'outperforms baselines across all metrics except ROUGE-L'. TED-F (lower better) 8.5 vs T5ParaBank1 8.4, so not best on that either.

results.claim: Sentence summarization on Gigaword: Impossible-T5 BERTScore-F1 85.1 vs ChatGPT 84.8, Referee 78.2.
results.setup: Gigaword; baselines ChatGPT, Referee (GPT3-distilled), T5 on ParaBank_summ
results.note: ROUGE-L 30.3 is below ChatGPT 33.6. No ChatGPT-distilled summarizer baseline in Table 5.

results.claim: Human evaluation on MRPC: Impossible-T5 faithfulness 2.55 vs ChatGPT 2.37 (3-level scale).
results.setup: 200 paraphrases per model, six MTurk workers, Krippendorff alpha 0.62
results.note: Fluent: Impossible-T5 2.74 vs ChatGPT 2.8, so ChatGPT is more fluent.

results.claim: On ParaSCI-arXiv Impossible-T5 outperforms ChatGPT on BERT-iBLEU.
results.table: Table 2, row Impossible-T5, column ParaSCI-arXiv B-iB (64.5) vs ChatGPT (63.9)

results.claim: Copy-Input scores state-of-the-art BLEU and ROUGE-L, so these metrics fail to assess paraphrase quality.
results.quote: a simple baseline that merely copies the input as an output (Copy-Input) marks state-of-the-art on these metrics, across all datasets.

results.claim: Paraphrastic proximity: sampled GPT2-XL continuations are more often mutually entailing with longer context and lower temperature; Self-BLEU stays around 32 for equivalent pairs.
results.setup: 1000 XSUM contexts of 1-5 sentences, 100 next sentences each, NLI both-direction entailment
results.quote: the average pair-wise Self-BLEU is around 32
results.note: Text prints '32' with footnote marker 1 (extracted as '321'). Human MRPC paraphrases average 39.

results.claim: Unsupervised baselines on Quora: Impossible-T5 iBLEU 16.40 vs MCPG 13.58.
results.table: Table 8, row Impossible-T5, column Quora iBLEU

limits: T5 fine-tuning hyperparameters (lr, batch size, epochs, optimizer) are not stated
Only sentence-level paraphrasing and summarization tested
Filters are frozen off-the-shelf critics; may not exist for other tasks
Distillation can inherit teacher bias and toxicity in open-ended settings
BLEU/ROUGE-L fail on paraphrase: Copy-Input is best
No seeds or significance tests; code and data release not stated in the text

terms.definition: LM's tendency to encode paraphrases on a proximal subspace in its distribution

Meng et al. 2021 indirectly uses paraphrastic proximity
